title: Palette Stripes
body:
Goal: build a list of colors and draw one labeled stripe for each.

The color-blind-safe (Okabe-Ito) colors:

name code
orange #E69F00
sky blue #56B4E9
bluish green #009E73
yellow #F0E442
blue #0072B2
vermillion #D55E00
reddish purple #CC79A7
black #000000
  1. Open starter.py and press Run: only one stripe appears.
  2. TODO 1: use palette.append(...) to add blue and vermillion.
  3. TODO 3: loop over the list with for i in range(len(colors)): and draw stripe i with label str(i). Move x along by width each time.
  4. TODO 4: print palette[0] and palette[-1].

Done looks like: a row of 5 or more stripes, labeled 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 ... Notice: the first stripe is number 0!

Extra: make the stripes thinner and use palette * 2 to draw the pattern twice.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run it and count the stripes. Only one shows up. Look at draw_stripes and see how many times draw_stripe is called. Also check how many colors build_palette makes.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: palette.append(x) adds one item to the end of a list. A for loop with range(len(colors)) gives you each index number, one at a time. Use that index to pick a color with square brackets. -1 means the last item.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Add with palette.append("____"). In the loop, use for i in range(len(____)):, then call draw_stripe(...) with colors[____] and str(____). Then add width to x. Print with palette[0] and palette[____].

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Palette Stripes
# Make a list of colors, then draw one stripe for each color.

import turtle


def build_palette():
    """Return a list of color-blind-safe (Okabe-Ito) colors."""
    palette = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73"]   # orange, sky blue, green
    # TODO 1: append blue "#0072B2" and vermillion "#D55E00" to the list.
    # TODO 2 (extra): append reddish purple "#CC79A7" too.
    return palette


def draw_stripe(t, x, y, width, height, color, label):
    """Draw one filled stripe with its top-left corner at (x, y) and a label under it."""
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.setheading(0)
    t.pendown()
    t.color("black", color)
    t.begin_fill()
    for side in [width, height, width, height]:
        t.forward(side)
        t.right(90)
    t.end_fill()
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x + width / 2, y - height - 25)
    t.write(label, align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))


def draw_stripes(t, colors, width=60):
    """Draw one stripe for every color in the list, left to right."""
    x = -len(colors) * width / 2          # start far enough left to center the stripes
    # TODO 3: this only draws stripe number 0. Use a loop:
    #   for i in range(len(colors)):
    # then draw stripe i (label str(i)) and move x along by width.
    draw_stripe(t, x, 100, width, 200, colors[0], "0")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    palette = build_palette()
    print(f"My palette has {len(palette)} colors.")
    # TODO 4: print the first color (index 0) and the last color (index -1).
    t = turtle.Turtle()
    t.speed(0)
    t.hideturtle()
    draw_stripes(t, palette)
    turtle.done()
